body.en: Deep factorisation of higher-degree polynomials without trial-and-error graphing, paired with the powerful Binomial Theorem for expanding \( (a+b)^n \) algebraically.

If a polynomial \( P(x) \) is divided by \( (ax - b) \), the remainder is \( R = P\left(\frac{b}{a}\right) \).
If \( P\left(\frac{b}{a}\right) = 0 \), then \( (ax - b) \) is an exact factor of \( P(x) \).

body.en:
Structural Decomposition Theorem: Any proper rational expression \(\dfrac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\) with \(\deg P < \deg Q\) over \(\mathbb{R}\) decomposes uniquely into a sum of simpler fractions determined by the factorization of \(Q(x)\). When \(\deg P \ge \deg Q\), Euclidean polynomial division yields \(\dfrac{P(x)}{Q(x)} = Q_{\text{quot}}(x) + \dfrac{R(x)}{Q(x)}\) with \(\deg R < \deg Q\).

For distinct linear factors \((x - a_1)(x - a_2)\), Heaviside's cover-up rule gives the exact residue \(A_k = \lim_{x \to a_k} (x - a_k)\dfrac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\). For a repeated factor \((x - a)^m\), all intermediate powers \((x - a)^1, (x - a)^2, \dots, (x - a)^m\) must be included to span the full \(m\)-dimensional rational subspace.

body.en:
Why Heaviside Cover-Up & Repeated-Factor Forms Work: Consider \(\dfrac{px + q}{(x - 4)(x + 6)} \equiv \dfrac{A}{x - 4} + \dfrac{B}{x + 6}\). Multiplying both sides by \((x - 4)(x + 6)\) yields the polynomial identity:

\[ px + q \equiv A(x + 6) + B(x - 4) \]

Because two polynomials equal on \(\mathbb{R} \setminus \{4, -6\}\) must be equal for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\) by continuity, setting \(x = 4\) annihilates the \(B\) term and isolates \(A = \dfrac{4p + q}{10}\). For a repeated root \((x - a)^2\), writing only \(\dfrac{B}{(x - a)^2}\) restricts the numerator to a constant \(B\), which cannot match a general linear numerator \(px + q\); adding \(\dfrac{A}{x - a}\) supplies \(A(x - a) + B\), spanning all degree-1 numerators.

problem.en: The polynomial \( P(x) = 2x^3 + ax^2 + bx - 6 \) has \( (x - 2) \) as a factor. When divided by \( (x + 1) \), the remainder is \( 12 \). Find the values of \( a \) and \( b \).

solution.en:
Step 1: Use Factor Theorem:
\( P(2) = 0 \implies 2(2)^3 + a(2)^2 + b(2) - 6 = 0 \implies 16 + 4a + 2b - 6 = 0 \implies 4a + 2b = -10 \implies 2a + b = -5 \) (Equation 1).
Step 2: Use Remainder Theorem:
\( P(-1) = 12 \implies 2(-1)^3 + a(-1)^2 + b(-1) - 6 = 12 \implies -2 + a - b - 6 = 12 \implies a - b = 20 \) (Equation 2).
Step 3: Solve simultaneously:
Add (1) and (2): \( (2a + b) + (a - b) = -5 + 20 \implies 3a = 15 \implies a = 5 \).
Substitute \( a = 5 \) into (2): \( 5 - b = 20 \implies b = -15 \).
Answer: \( a = 5, \, b = -15 \).

label.en: Worked Example \(B\) — Polynomials, Remainder Theorem & Binomial Theorem (Easy Application)

problem.en: Find the remainder when the polynomial \( f(x) = 4x^3 - 6x^2 + 3x - 1 \) is divided by \( 2x - 1 \).

solution.en: By the Remainder Theorem, when a polynomial \( f(x) \) is divided by a linear factor of the form \( ax - b \), the remainder is \( f\left(\frac{b}{a}\right) \). Here, the divisor is \( 2x - 1 \), so we set \( 2x - 1 = 0 \implies x = \frac{1}{2} \). Substitute \( x = \frac{1}{2} \) into \( f(x) \): \[ f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 4\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 - 6\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + 3\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) - 1 \] \[ = 4\left(\frac{1}{8}\right) - 6\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) + \frac{3}{2} - 1 \] \[ = \frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{2} + \frac{3}{2} - 1 = -\frac{1}{2} \] Therefore, the remainder is \( -\frac{1}{2} \).

label.en: Worked Example \(C\) — Polynomials, Remainder Theorem & Binomial Theorem (Medium Application)

problem.en:
The polynomial \( P(x) = 2x^3 + ax^2 + bx - 6 \) has a factor of \( x - 2 \) and leaves a remainder of \( -24 \) when divided by \( x + 1 \), where \( a \) and \( b \) are constants.

Find the remainder when \( P(x) \) is divided by \( x - 3 \).

solution.en: Step 1: Use the Factor Theorem for the factor \( x - 2 \). Since \( x - 2 \) is a factor, \( P(2) = 0 \): \[ P(2) = 2(2)^3 + a(2)^2 + b(2) - 6 = 0 \] \[ 16 + 4a + 2b - 6 = 0 \implies 4a + 2b = -10 \implies 2a + b = -5 \quad \text{--- (1)} \] Step 2: Use the Remainder Theorem for division by \( x + 1 \). Since the remainder is \( -24 \), \( P(-1) = -24 \): \[ P(-1) = 2(-1)^3 + a(-1)^2 + b(-1) - 6 = -24 \] \[ -2 + a - b - 6 = -24 \implies a - b - 8 = -24 \implies a - b = -16 \quad \text{--- (2)} \] Step 3: Solve the simultaneous equations. Adding (1) and (2): \[ (2a + b) + (a - b) = -5 + (-16) \] \[ 3a = -21 \implies a = -7 \] Substitute \( a = -7 \) into (2): \[ -7 - b = -16 \implies b = 9 \] Thus, the polynomial is: \[ P(x) = 2x^3 - 7x^2 + 9x - 6 \] Step 4: Find the remainder when \( P(x) \) is divided by \( x - 3 \). By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder is \( P(3) \): \[ P(3) = 2(3)^3 - 7(3)^2 + 9(3) - 6 = 2(27) - 7(9) + 27 - 6 = 54 - 63 + 27 - 6 = 12 \]

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Polynomials, Remainder Theorem & Binomial Theorem (Hard Application)

problem.en:
In the expansion of \((1 + ax)^n\) in ascending powers of \(x\), the coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(60\) and the coefficient of \(x^3\) is \(160\), where \(n\) is a positive integer and \(a > 0\).

A cubic polynomial \(P(x)\), in which the coefficient of \(x^3\) is \(1\), has \((x - a)^2\) as a factor and leaves a remainder of \(n\) when divided by \((x - 1)\).

Find the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x + a)\).

solution.en: Step 1: Determine \(n\) and \(a\) using the Binomial Theorem. In the expansion of \((1 + ax)^n\): \[ \text{Term in } x^2 = \binom{n}{2} (ax)^2 = \frac{n(n - 1)}{2} a^2 x^2 = 60 x^2 \implies n(n - 1)a^2 = 120 \] \[ \text{Term in } x^3 = \binom{n}{3} (ax)^3 = \frac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)}{6} a^3 x^3 = 160 x^3 \implies n(n - 1)(n - 2)a^3 = 960 \] Dividing the equation for \(x^3\) by the equation for \(x^2\): \[ \frac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)a^3}{n(n - 1)a^2} = \frac{960}{120} \implies (n - 2)a = 8 \implies a = \frac{8}{n - 2} \] Substitute \(a = \frac{8}{n - 2}\) into \(n(n - 1)a^2 = 120\): \[ n(n - 1) \left(\frac{8}{n - 2}\right)^2 = 120 \implies \frac{64n(n - 1)}{(n - 2)^2} = 120 \] Dividing both sides by \(8\): \[ \frac{8n(n - 1)}{(n - 2)^2} = 15 \implies 8(n^2 - n) = 15(n^2 - 4n + 4) \] \[ 8n^2 - 8n = 15n^2 - 60n + 60 \implies 7n^2 - 52n + 60 = 0 \] Factoring the quadratic: \[ (7n - 30)(n - 6) = 0 \] Since \(n\) must be a positive integer, we have \(n = 6\). Then \(a = \frac{8}{6 - 2} = \frac{8}{4} = 2\). Step 2: Determine the polynomial \(P(x)\). Since \(P(x)\) is a cubic polynomial with leading coefficient \(1\) and has \((x - a)^2 = (x - 2)^2\) as a factor, it can be written as: \[ P(x) = (x - 2)^2 (x - c) \] for some constant \(c\). By the Remainder Theorem, the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x - 1)\) is \(P(1)\): \[ P(1) = (1 - 2)^2 (1 - c) = 1 \cdot (1 - c) = 1 - c \] Given that this remainder is \(n = 6\): \[ 1 - c = 6 \implies c = -5 \] Thus, \(P(x) = (x - 2)^2 (x + 5)\). Step 3: Evaluate the remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x + a) = (x + 2)\). By the Remainder Theorem, the required remainder is \(P(-2)\): \[ P(-2) = (-2 - 2)^2 (-2 + 5) = (-4)^2 \cdot 3 = 16 \cdot 3 = 48 \]

body.en:
1. Skipping Division on Equal-Degree Fractions: On Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics (0606), expressions like \(\dfrac{x^2 + 4x + 1}{(x - 1)(x + 6)}\) have \(\deg P = \deg Q = 2\). Setting this equal to \(\dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 6}\) without adding the leading constant \(+ 1\) loses 2–3 method and accuracy marks immediately.

2. Irreducible Quadratic Numerators: When the denominator contains an irreducible quadratic factor \(x^2 + 6\), the numerator template must be linear \(\dfrac{Bx + C}{x^2 + 6}\), never a single constant \(\dfrac{B}{x^2 + 6}\).

question.en: [Practice 1 · Easy] When the polynomial \(\mathrm{P}(x) = 2x^3 - 3x^2 + ax - 8\) is divided by \(x - 3\), the remainder is \(10\). What is the value of the constant \(a\)?

hints.en: According to the Remainder Theorem, when a polynomial \(\mathrm{P}(x)\) is divided by \(x - c\), the remainder is equal to \(\mathrm{P}(c)\).

Here, the divisor is \(x - 3\), so \(c = 3\). We evaluate \(\mathrm{P}(3)\): \(\mathrm{P}(3) = 2(3)^3 - 3(3)^2 + a(3) - 8\) \(\mathrm{P}(3) = 2(27) - 3(9) + 3a - 8 = 54 - 27 + 3a - 8 = 19 + 3a\) Given that the remainder is \(10\): \(19 + 3a = 10\).
Use the resulting form to finish: \(3a = 10 - 19\).

solution.en:
According to the Remainder Theorem, when a polynomial \(\mathrm{P}(x)\) is divided by \(x - c\), the remainder is equal to \(\mathrm{P}(c)\).

Here, the divisor is \(x - 3\), so \(c = 3\). We evaluate \(\mathrm{P}(3)\):
\[
\mathrm{P}(3) = 2(3)^3 - 3(3)^2 + a(3) - 8
\]
\[
\mathrm{P}(3) = 2(27) - 3(9) + 3a - 8 = 54 - 27 + 3a - 8 = 19 + 3a
\]

Given that the remainder is \(10\):
\[
19 + 3a = 10
\]
\[
3a = 10 - 19 = -9
\]
\[
a = -3
\]

question.en: [Practice 2 · Medium] In the expansion of \((1 + ax)^n\) in ascending powers of \(x\), where \(n\) is a positive integer and \(a\) is a constant, the coefficient of \(x\) is \(-12\) and the coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(60\). Find the coefficient of \(x^3\).

hints.en: Using the binomial theorem, the expansion of \((1 + ax)^n\) is given by: \((1 + ax)^n = 1 + \binom{n}{1}(ax) + \binom{n}{2}(ax)^2 + \binom{n}{3}(ax)^3 + \dots\).
Equate the coefficient of \(x\): \(\binom{n}{1}a = na = -12 \implies a = -\frac{12}{n}\) Equate the coefficient of \(x^2\): \(\binom{n}{2}a^2 = \frac{n(n - 1)}{2} a^2 = 60 \implies n(n - 1)a^2\).

solution.en:
Using the binomial theorem, the expansion of \((1 + ax)^n\) is given by:
\[
(1 + ax)^n = 1 + \binom{n}{1}(ax) + \binom{n}{2}(ax)^2 + \binom{n}{3}(ax)^3 + \dots
\]

1. **Equate the coefficient of \(x\):**
\[
\binom{n}{1}a = na = -12 \implies a = -\frac{12}{n}
\]

2. **Equate the coefficient of \(x^2\):**
\[
\binom{n}{2}a^2 = \frac{n(n - 1)}{2} a^2 = 60 \implies n(n - 1)a^2 = 120
\]
Substitute \(a = -\frac{12}{n}\):
\[
n(n - 1)\left(-\frac{12}{n}\right)^2 = 120
\]
\[
n(n - 1) \cdot \frac{144}{n^2} = 120 \implies \frac{n - 1}{n} = \frac{120}{144} = \frac{5}{6}
\]
Solving for \(n\):
\[
6(n - 1) = 5n \implies 6n - 6 = 5n \implies n = 6
\]
Then, find \(a\):
\[
a = -\frac{12}{6} = -2
\]

3. **Calculate the coefficient of \(x^3\):**
\[
\text{Coefficient of } x^3 = \binom{n}{3}a^3 = \binom{6}{3}(-2)^3 = 20 \times (-8) = -160
\]

question.en: [Practice 3 · Easy] The polynomial \( p(x) = 2x^3 + ax^2 - 5x + 6 \) is divisible by \( x - 2 \). Find the value of the constant \( a \).

hints.en: By the Factor Theorem, if \( p(x) \) is divisible by \( x - 2 \), then \( p(2) = 0 \).

solution.en:
By the Factor Theorem, if \( p(x) \) is divisible by \( x - 2 \), then \( p(2) = 0 \).

Substitute \( x = 2 \) into the polynomial expression:
\[ p(2) = 2(2)^3 + a(2)^2 - 5(2) + 6 \]
\[ p(2) = 2(8) + 4a - 10 + 6 = 16 + 4a - 10 + 6 = 4a + 12 \]

Setting \( p(2) = 0 \):
\[ 4a + 12 = 0 \implies 4a = -12 \implies a = -3 \]

label.en: ● Master Atlas of the 9 Main Parent Functions & Universal Transformation Law

body.en:
Every algebraic and elementary transcendental model is built by transforming one of the nine core parent functions via \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\), where \(|a|\) scales vertically (reflecting across the \(x\)-axis if \(a < 0\)), \(h\) shifts horizontally, and \(k\) shifts vertically:

FamilyTransformed Form \(g(x)\)DomainRange (\(a > 0\))Key Geometric Feature
Constant\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)Horizontal line, slope \(0\)
Linear\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Constant slope \(m = a\), pivot \((h, k)\)
Quadratic\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Parabola vertex \((h, k)\), axis \(x = h\)
Cubic\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Inflection center \((h, k)\), S-curve
Absolute Value\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)V-corner vertex \((h, k)\), slopes \(\pm a\)
Radical\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Endpoint \((h, k)\), half-parabola
Rational\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), horizontal \(y = k\)
Exponential\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)Horizontal asymptote \(y = k\), anchor \((h, a+k)\)
Logarithmic\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), anchor \((h+1, k)\)
